## What's new
- **Share through Cloudflare, on your own domain.** Pick Cloudflare in Settings › Sharing, sign in once, and type a domain of yours that's on Cloudflare: billing.localhost is shared at billing.yourdomain.com, the same address every time, with no warning page for visitors. ngrok works as before. Cloudflare's free plan isn't for serving video or mostly large files. - **A redesigned menu.** Names come first. Click a row to open it; copy, share and details appear when you point at it. Each server's details, renaming and sharing are on a page of their own instead of popovers. - **Find and move with the keyboard.** Type to filter by name, port, process or image. ↑↓ choose a row, Return opens it, → or ⌘Return shows its details, ⌘C copies its address, ⌘S shares it, Esc clears the filter. - **A Settings window** (⌘,) for the proxy, HTTPS, sharing, notifications and your license. It shows whether the proxy got ports 80 and 443, and offers to try again when it didn't. - **Apps' and macOS's listeners** are folded into one Other Listeners group at the bottom, out of the way. - **Setting up HTTPS** is offered once, from the menu, until you do it or dismiss it.
Sharing is part of a license, and of the 14-day trial.

## What's new
- **Share a server with someone outside your network.** Right-click a named server and choose Share, or press Share… in its name editor. Nametag gives you a private link through ngrok, on your own ngrok account: install it (`brew install ngrok`) and sign in once. - **Only people with the link get in.** It lasts an hour, four hours or until you stop it, and the panel shows who visited. A globe in the menu bar means something is shared. - **Warnings before sharing a debugger.** Nametag checks whether visitors would see Flask's debugger, Django's DEBUG pages or the Django Debug Toolbar, and says how to turn them off. - **About Nametag** in the gear menu.
Sharing is part of a license, and of the 14-day trial.

## What's new
- **Licenses.** Nametag now has a free version and a paid one. Every feature is unlocked for 14 days from the first launch of this version. After that, the free version keeps finding and diagnosing everything and serves 3 web names over HTTP (databases and caches don't count). A license adds every name, HTTPS, notifications and the cookie fix, on up to 3 Macs, and covers every version released within a year of purchase. Buy one, or enter your key, from the license item in the gear menu. - **Names past the free limit** open on their ports, with a lock on their rows; visiting one shows a page with a link to the port. - **Cookie diagnosis for everyone.** The free version still tells you which cookies a browser refuses and which setting to change in the app.
